title: POFMA Office's Actions In Regard To Misinformation about COVID-19 and COVID-19 Vaccination
what_it_is: POFMA Office's Actions In Regard To Misinformation about COVID-19 and COVID-19 Vaccination

sections.label: COVID-19 misinformation responses and public education
sections.summary: The Government responded to over 60 COVID-19 falsehoods using public communications and POFMA, focusing on accurate updates and public education to build vaccine resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In the past year, we have responded to over 60 instances of speculation, rumours, scams and outright falsehoods pertaining to COVID-19, using a range of responses – from public communications to legislative levers, including the Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act or POFMA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: A key focus of the Ministerial Taskforce and our Government agencies has been to provide accurate updates from trusted sources in a timely and transparent manner, to help ensure our citizens are well-informed and to calm anxieties caused by such misinformation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Public education is key to our vaccination programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We want to strengthen our resilience against vaccine misinformation by enhancing the understanding of COVID-19 vaccines and debunking falsehoods, so that Singaporeans can make informed decisions for the safety and health of themselves, their loved ones and the community.

sections.label: Media, tech and volunteer outreach
sections.summary: Local media, tech companies, People's Association volunteers and Silver Generation Ambassadors helped address vaccine queries, with legal action used where warranted.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The local media has also published articles and FAQ columns to address concerns and questions about vaccines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We have also worked with major tech companies to ensure that authoritative sources, including MOH’s website, are prominently included on their platforms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: As we commence the vaccination programme for seniors, community volunteers from the People’s Association, as well as Silver Generation Ambassadors, will be conducting house visits to speak to our seniors and address their queries about the COVID-19 vaccine and the vaccination programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Where there is cause for action, we will not hesitate to use the full force of the law.

sections.label: Range of responses to misinformation
sections.summary: Responses range from public education to clarification and engagement with parties, with legislative levers used only when circumstances warrant.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In our response to misinformation as I have described, we have a range of possibilities – from public education, to a targeted effort to clarify a particular point on Government websites and other channels, as well as working with the specific parties concerned.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: We do not need to always resort to the extreme use of the legislative levers, unless it is warranted by the circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Therefore, in the kind of example that the Member cites, very often, we have found that engagement with the relevant parties has sufficed to clarify the matter and correct the misinformation.
